title: Bad Guys Finish First: Philly Topples the HULK as Javonte Williams Cashes In on Day One
dek: Team Pillbert hands No Banner only HULK its first loss, Zoe stuns the Horse, the Habibsters wake up with 140 and the top of the table becomes a four-way logjam at 3-1.
body: The unbeaten run is over, and of course it was Alan who ended it. Team Pillbert beat Ramon's No Banner only HULK 125.42 to 116.72 as a 29% underdog, and the man who did the most damage arrived a week ago. Javonte Williams, freshly acquired from Randy, posted 28.8 points on a 13.25 projection in his Pillbert debut. Brucie got 30.4 from Kenneth Walker III and still lost, which tells you how much went right on the other side. Philly is now 3-1 on a three-game win streak, and his title odds jumped from 9% to 21%, the biggest climb in the league.

The scary part for everyone else is that Alan left points on the table and won anyway. Kyle Monangai scored 27.5 from the Team Pillbert bench on a 7.57 projection, more than three times the final margin. Then Philly went shopping like a man who thinks he's a contender. He moved Ashton Jeanty in from JMoney for Isaiah Likely, Emeka Egbuka and Denzel Boston, then flipped Jeanty and Davante Adams to Mekhi for Justin Jefferson. He also cut De'Von Achane and Bryce Young and added Tyreek Hill, Ollie Gordon II, Kalif Raymond and kicker Spencer Shrader. That's a whole new roster built around one blockbuster, and next week he plays the guy who got Jeanty and Adams.

Upset number two came from Zoe. Ghostu-Spider SZN beat Sonny's The Horse is Hea 120.88 to 95.1 as a 30% underdog, and Tetairoa McMillan was the reason: 38.2 points on a 13.5 projection, the top score of the week. Bijan Robinson added 27.2, and Zilgit could afford to leave Nico Collins and his 27.3 on the bench. She's back to 2-2, swapped Kyler Murray for Jared Goff this week, and has climbed into fifth. Her title odds only crept from 1% to 2%, but nobody in the bottom half has more momentum right now.

Sonny's week was the reverse image. Chuba Hubbard, the back he traded Rashee Rice for, scored 25.4 in his Horse debut, all of it from the bench. The Horse lost by 25.78, so Hubbard alone wouldn't quite have saved it, but Parker Washington's 1.5 on a 12.79 projection in the lineup made the decision sting more. Sonny went back to the wire hard, adding Tony Pollard for J.K. Dobbins, Juwan Johnson, the Bears D/ST and Bryce Young, the quarterback Alan cut that same week, while letting Mark Andrews go. Title odds fell from 21% to 11%, but at 3-1 with 67% playoff odds, the Horse is wobbling, not falling.

Habib finally showed up. The Habibsters dropped 140.1 on Randy's The fumblers, the highest score of the week, winning by 43.22 despite a 39% pregame chance. CeeDee Lamb went for 32.8 on a 13.65 projection, and Kaushal now has 459.1 points for, more than three of the 3-1 teams' rivals and actually more than Randy's 458.7. The two-time champ remade his roster on the fly, with Sam Darnold in for Drake Maye, Braelon Allen in for Kyle Pitts Sr., Keenan Allen added and a Vikings D/ST swap. His title odds jumped from 1% to 8%. At 1-3 the record still looks rough, but the points say this team should be a lot better than that.

Kai got his first win too, as the Dawgs beat Jordan's Counting or not Counting GV 107.54 to 90.22. Kyren Williams carried it with 31.7 on an 11.88 projection, which was badly needed after Ja'Marr Chase posted 4.2 on a 16.54 projection. Mekhi now has Jeanty and Adams on the roster and Team Pillbert next on the schedule, which is about as juicy as a week 5 matchup gets. JMoney falls to 0-4 with 0% playoff odds after Garrett Wilson's 4.2, and his roster churn continued: Kirk Cousins in for Marvin Harrison Jr., Dalton Schultz in for Michael Pittman Jr., Michael Wilson in for Tank Bigsby, plus the Jeanty sale to Alan. It reads like a manager rebuilding mid-performance.

The standings are a four-way tie at 3-1: No Banner only HULK, Team Pillbert, The Horse is Hea and The fumblers, separated only by points. Ramon still leads with 561 points, 80.1 clear of Philly, and 41% title odds, down from 52% but still nearly double anyone else. Randy's title odds slipped again, from 16% to 14%, and Stefon Diggs gave him 6 in his debut while the guy he traded away went for 28.8. Behind the top four sit Ghostu-Spider SZN at 2-2, then the Habibsters and Dawgs at 1-3, all with a pulse and all facing a crowded logjam above them.

Week 5 is loaded. Mekhi hosts Philly in the Jeanty-and-Adams reunion special, a chance for Kai to beat Alan with the pieces Alan just shipped him. Brucie tries to start a new streak against Randy, Zoe looks to climb back above .500 against a winless JMoney, and Habib gets Sonny in a game that will tell us whether the 140 was a breakout or a blip. Four teams at 3-1, ten weeks left, and only four playoff spots.

social.author: Team Pillbert
social.text: Three straight wins and the HULK goes down! Player of the week: Javonte Williams, 28.8 in his debut. And welcome to the club, Justin Jefferson. Dawgs next. 🏈

social.author: Marcus Pell
social.text: Alan won the Diggs trade by 22.8 points in week one, beat the best team in the league, then traded half his roster for Justin Jefferson. You don't have to like it. You do have to take Team Pillbert seriously now.

social.author: Ghostu-Spider SZN Fan Club

trade_watch.take: It looked like an Alan win on paper and it looks worse for Randy after one week: Javonte Williams dropped 28.8 in Philly's upset of the HULK while Stefon Diggs managed 6. A 22.8-point gap in the debut week is the kind of number Randy will be hearing about for a while.

Both sides fumbled the debut. Chuba Hubbard scored 25.4 for Sonny, all of it on the bench in a loss, while Rashee Rice gave Brucie zero from the bench in another loss, so neither unbeaten got a single lineup point out of the deal.

bios.1: Sonny's 3-1 squad lost to Zoe with Chuba Hubbard's 25.4 stuck on the bench, and the title odds were cut nearly in half to 11%. Busy on the wire with Pollard, Juwan Johnson and Bryce Young, and still holding 67% playoff odds.
bios.2: Randy got run over 140.1 to 96.88 by the Habibsters and watched his title odds slide for the fourth straight week, now 14%. Still 3-1, though, and he reworked the roster with Trevor Lawrence, Darren Waller and Jordan Addison.
bios.3: JMoney is 0-4 with 0% playoff odds after losing to the Dawgs. He's reshaping the roster with Kirk Cousins, Dalton Schultz, Michael Wilson and a three-player haul from the Jeanty trade, so the rest of the season is about building something new.
bios.4: Three straight wins, an upset of the HULK and a title-odds jump from 9% to 21%. Alan then rebuilt the roster around Justin Jefferson, and now gets to face the Dawgs team holding the pieces he traded away.
bios.5: Mekhi's first win came on Kyren Williams' 31.7, surviving a 4.2 from Ja'Marr Chase. Kai traded Justin Jefferson for Ashton Jeanty and Davante Adams, and the first test is against the man who sent them over.
bios.6: Kaushal snapped the losing streak with the week's top score, 140.1, led by CeeDee Lamb's 32.8. At 1-3 with more points than two of the 3-1 teams, the two-time champ looks a lot better than his record.
bios.7: Ramon's juggernaut finally lost, falling to Team Pillbert despite Kenneth Walker III's 30.4. Still leads the league with 561 points and 41% title odds, so one bad Sunday hasn't changed who the favorite is.
bios.8: Zoe stunned the Horse behind Tetairoa McMillan's league-best 38.2 and Bijan Robinson's 27.2 to get back to 2-2. Jared Goff is the new quarterback, and fifth place with 18% playoff odds is a real foothold.
